metadata.description: Test cases to verify KB retrieval and hallucination detection with mixed labels (SAFE, ABSTAIN, FLAGGED)

test_cases.claim: The Information Technology Act, 2000 is Act No. 21 of 2000
The IT Act 2000 received presidential assent on 9th June, 2000
Section 65 deals with tampering with computer source documents
Section 66 covers computer related offences punishable with imprisonment up to three years
Section 66A was struck down by the Supreme Court in Shreya Singhal vs Union of India case
Section 66B deals with punishment for dishonestly receiving stolen computer resource or communication device
Section 66C covers punishment for identity theft with imprisonment up to three years
Section 66D deals with cheating by personation using computer resource
Section 66E covers punishment for violation of privacy
Section 66F deals with cyber terrorism and punishment can extend to life imprisonment
Section 67 covers publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form
Section 67A deals with sexually explicit content with punishment up to five years on first conviction
Section 67B covers material depicting children in sexually explicit acts
Section 67C mandates intermediaries to preserve and retain information
Section 69 gives power to government for interception or monitoring of information
Section 69A provides power to issue directions for blocking public access to information
Section 69B authorizes monitoring and collecting traffic data for cyber security
Section 70 deals with protected systems and critical information infrastructure
Section 70A designates a national nodal agency for critical information infrastructure protection
Section 70B establishes the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
Section 43 provides for penalty and compensation for damage to computer systems
Section 43A covers compensation for failure to protect data
The Act extends to the whole of India and applies to offences committed outside India
Section 79 provides exemption from liability for intermediaries in certain cases
The Act came into force on 17th October, 2000
Electronic signature is defined in Section 3A of the Act
Section 4 provides legal recognition to electronic records
Section 5 provides legal recognition to electronic signatures
The Controller of Certifying Authorities is appointed under Section 17
Section 21 covers licensing requirements for issuing electronic signature certificates
The Appellate Tribunal is the TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal)
Section 78 states that police officers not below the rank of Inspector can investigate offences
Section 80 gives police officers power to enter and search public places without warrant
The First Schedule lists documents to which the Act does not apply
Negotiable instruments other than cheques are excluded from the Act's application
Power of attorney documents are excluded from the Act except when explicitly digitally signed
test_cases.reason: Core claim is accurate - power of attorney is excluded. Minor exception detail doesn't materially change truthfulness.

test_cases.claim: Wills and testamentary dispositions are excluded from the Act unless filed electronically with courts
test_cases.reason: Core claim is accurate - wills are excluded. Exception is interpretive, doesn't create major falsehood.

test_cases.claim: Contracts for sale of immovable property are excluded from the Act except for commercial properties above Rs 1 crore
test_cases.reason: Partial truth: Contracts for immovable property are excluded, but the commercial property exception is fabricated

test_cases.claim: Computer contaminant means instructions designed to modify, destroy or usurp normal operation, including AI algorithms that cause system slowdowns
test_cases.reason: Partial truth: First part is accurate, but AI algorithm addition is anachronistic

test_cases.claim: Computer virus is defined as instruction that damages or degrades computer resource performance, with penalties starting at Rs 5 lakhs
test_cases.reason: Definition is correct. Penalty detail, while potentially inaccurate, doesn't negate core definition.

test_cases.claim: Section 72 covers penalty for breach of confidentiality and privacy with mandatory reporting to Data Protection Authority
test_cases.reason: Section 72 correctly covers confidentiality breach. DPA reference is anachronistic but doesn't negate main claim.

test_cases.claim: Section 72A deals with disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract and applies to both private and government employees
test_cases.reason: Section 72A description is accurate. Scope statement is interpretive, not materially false.

test_cases.claim: The Act was amended by the Information Technology Amendment Act 2008 (Act 10 of 2009) and further amended in 2015
test_cases.reason: 2008 amendment is correct. 2015 reference may be Rules/Guidelines, not materially false.

test_cases.claim: Cyber cafe is defined as a facility offering internet access to public in ordinary course of business and must register with local police
test_cases.reason: Definition is correct. Registration requirement may be from Rules/local laws, not core IT Act.

test_cases.claim: Cyber security means protecting information and devices from unauthorized access and disruption, with ISO 27001 certification mandatory for government systems
test_cases.reason: Definition is correct. ISO certification may be from separate policy, not IT Act itself.

test_cases.claim: Intermediary includes telecom providers, ISPs, web hosts, search engines and online marketplaces, all of which must obtain annual licenses from MEITY
test_cases.reason: Definition is correct, but blanket licensing requirement is fabricated

test_cases.claim: Section 84A allows Central Government to prescribe modes for encryption with minimum 256-bit key length
test_cases.reason: Section 84A on encryption is correct. Specific bit-length is technical detail, doesn't negate main claim.

test_cases.claim: Section 85 covers offences by companies and liability of directors, who can face up to 10 years imprisonment
test_cases.reason: Section 85 description is accurate. Specific imprisonment term is detail variation.

test_cases.claim: The Cyber Regulations Advisory Committee is constituted under Section 88 with members from all state governments
test_cases.reason: Committee under Section 88 is correct. Composition detail is administrative, not core claim.

test_cases.claim: Section 81 states the Act has overriding effect over other laws except the Indian Penal Code
test_cases.reason: Overriding effect is correct. IPC exception is interpretive/contextual.

test_cases.claim: Section 66 covers computer related offences but excludes white-collar crimes involving computers
test_cases.reason: Section 66 on computer offences is correct. Exclusion statement is interpretive.

test_cases.claim: Section 69 gives power to government for interception or monitoring of information only during national emergencies
test_cases.reason: Section 69 on interception is correct. Emergency limitation is contextual interpretation.

test_cases.claim: Section 67A deals with sexually explicit content with punishment up to five years on first conviction and mandatory life imprisonment on third conviction
test_cases.reason: First part is accurate. Repeat offense enhancement is plausible legal interpretation.

test_cases.claim: Section 43A covers compensation for failure to protect data and creates personal criminal liability for CEOs
test_cases.reason: Section 43A is civil compensation, not criminal. CEO liability claim is material misrepresentation.

test_cases.claim: The Act came into force on 17th October, 2000 across all Indian states and union territories except Jammu & Kashmir
test_cases.reason: Date is correct. J&K exception was historically accurate (Article 370 context).

test_cases.claim: Section 66G deals with punishment for online fraud and carries imprisonment up to 5 years
test_cases.reason: Section 66G does not exist in IT Act 2000

test_cases.claim: The IT Act 2000 mandates all companies to conduct annual cyber security audits
test_cases.reason: No such blanket mandatory requirement in the Act

test_cases.claim: Section 68A provides for establishment of a National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
test_cases.reason: Section 68A does not exist in the Act

test_cases.claim: Under IT Act 2000, all digital payments above Rs 10,000 require two-factor authentication
test_cases.reason: Act does not specify such payment thresholds or authentication requirements

test_cases.claim: The Act mandates that all government websites must use .gov.in domain only
test_cases.reason: No such domain mandate in the Act

test_cases.claim: Section 71A deals with unauthorized access to social media accounts
test_cases.reason: Section 71A does not exist; Section 71 covers misrepresentation only

test_cases.claim: The IT Act requires all emails to be encrypted with AES-256 encryption
test_cases.reason: Act does not mandate specific encryption standards for emails

test_cases.claim: Section 44A provides compensation for victims of online defamation
test_cases.reason: Section 44A does not exist in the Act

test_cases.claim: The Act established a Cyber Crime Victim Compensation Fund managed by CERT-In
test_cases.reason: No such fund mentioned in the Act

test_cases.claim: Under Section 75A, sharing of personal data requires explicit written consent in physical form
test_cases.reason: Section 75A does not exist; Act predates modern data protection concepts

test_cases.claim: The IT Act mandates biometric authentication for all financial transactions above Rs 50,000
test_cases.reason: No such biometric mandate in the Act

test_cases.claim: Section 82A establishes a Digital Evidence Forensic Laboratory in every state
test_cases.reason: Section 82A does not exist; only Section 82 exists

test_cases.claim: The Act requires all mobile apps to register with the Ministry of Electronics and IT before launch
test_cases.reason: No app registration requirement in the Act

test_cases.claim: Section 66H covers unauthorized cryptocurrency mining with penalty up to Rs 10 lakhs
test_cases.reason: Section 66H does not exist; Act predates cryptocurrency

test_cases.claim: The IT Act mandates data localization requiring all user data to be stored within India
test_cases.reason: No data localization mandate in the Act
